title: CLI Review Specification
purpose: Run an opencode review of the repository against the code, architecture, or prose standards.

requirements.name: Command Form
requirements.body: The system SHALL accept a scope of `code`, `architecture`, or `prose` for the review command.

scenarios.name: Code scope
steps: THEN it reviews the repository against the code guidelines

scenarios.name: Architecture scope
steps: THEN it reviews the repository against the architecture guidelines

scenarios.name: Prose scope
steps: THEN it reviews the repository against the prose guidelines

scenarios.name: Unknown scope
steps: GIVEN a scope the command does not name
THEN it errors and reviews nothing

requirements.name: Repository Scope
requirements.body: The system SHALL review the repository the command runs in.

scenarios.name: Nested invocation
steps: GIVEN the command runs in a subdirectory of a git repository
THEN it reviews the repository at its root

requirements.name: Model Option
requirements.body: The system SHALL accept a `--model` option and forward its value to opencode. When the user gives no value, the model is `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`.

scenarios.name: Default model
steps: THEN opencode runs with the model `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`

scenarios.name: Custom model
steps: THEN opencode runs with that model

requirements.name: Variant Option
requirements.body: The system SHALL accept a `--variant` option and forward its value to opencode. When the user gives no `--model`, the variant defaults to `high`; when the user gives a `--model`, the variant carries no value.

scenarios.name: Default variant
steps: THEN opencode runs with the variant `high`

scenarios.name: Model picks the variant
steps: THEN opencode runs with no variant

scenarios.name: Explicit variant
steps: THEN opencode runs with the variant `minimal`

requirements.name: Code Review
requirements.body: The system SHALL prompt opencode to write each code issue it finds to a `refactor-<slug>.yaml` project rather than editing the code.

scenarios.name: Issue becomes a project
steps: AND opencode finds a code issue

scenarios.name: Existing project is updated
steps: AND a matching `refactor-<slug>.yaml` project already exists
AND opencode finds another issue in the same refactor
THEN the existing project gains the issue

scenarios.name: No issues
steps: AND opencode finds no code issues
THEN no refactor project is written

requirements.name: Architecture Review
requirements.body: The system SHALL prompt opencode to write each architecture issue it finds to a `refactor-<slug>.yaml` project rather than editing the code.

scenarios.name: Issue becomes a project
steps: AND opencode finds an architecture issue

requirements.name: Prose Review
requirements.body: The system SHALL prompt opencode to fix each prose issue it finds immediately.

scenarios.name: Issue is fixed
steps: AND opencode finds a prose issue
THEN the offending text is edited in place
